writings.author: Thomas
writings.scope: Dissent on statutory classification and judgment

law_summary: Federal habeas courts independently decide whether the established interrogation circumstances amount to Miranda custody. Section 2254(d)'s factual presumption, all eight exceptions and its conditional convincing-evidence burden remain applicable to historical findings. Neither review classification nor remand establishes custody, a constitutional violation, harmlessness or a right to the writ.
published_positions: Thomas would treat the concrete reasonable-person custody inference as presumptively factual under §2254(d) while reviewing the legal definition independently. He would affirm on classification, without a new no-custody, retroactivity or harmlessness determination.
next_stage: Remand to the Ninth Circuit for independent ultimate custody review and such further proper habeas proceedings as are necessary; no immediate release or further Supreme Court event is set.
